checks: The endpoint product is compact. Nonnegative measures on it of mass bounded by the common uniform bound form a nonempty weakly compact metrizable space, including the zero measure. Take a common compact physical test set containing the old and ceiling supports and the barycentric image of the entire product.

On the fixed supports, the marginal tests by absolute difference and the ceiling tests against a dense family of nonnegative continuous functions are Borel in the parameter and continuous in the candidate measure. Uniform approximation, bounded masses and uniqueness and positivity of finite measures determined by continuous tests give exactly the required equalities and domination.

A finite convex function on the whole Euclidean space is continuous and has a supporting affine function at each point. The relatively open sets where those affine functions are within a fixed tolerance cover the common compact set. The finite subcover maximum and then rational coefficient approximation give uniform approximation there. Mass equality is imposed separately. Signed affine tests both ways give first-moment equality with the actual old kernel.

The feasible domain is Borel and contains the full-measure pointwise feasibility set. Weak Borel measurability of the selector implies Borel evaluation on every Borel set by a monotone class argument. Fixed marginal equalities give any marginal support restrictions, including varying ones, on the same feasible set.

For a joint Borel event, its sections are Borel and conditional domination integrates to joint domination. Jointly Borel convex tests bounded on the common compact set are integrable under both old and output laws. On the common full-measure set convex order already holds for every finite convex test, so selecting a section introduces no new exceptional set. A jointly Borel output support condition shared by all feasible choices almost everywhere then integrates to zero mass of its complement.

The ceiling is imposed on the selected barycentric output for the prescribed old-law comparison. The argument preserves the specified marginal masses and any already valid aggregate bound on repeated endpoint occurrences. It uses joint pointwise feasibility as a hypothesis.
Read archived source 5ea88513a25f2f4b §§1–2 and verified its raw digest. The frozen constraints are explicit about equal mass and cover the source's localized comparison and joint support.

dependencies.mapping: Use the fixed nonempty compact metric space of bounded nonnegative tuple measures and the jointly Borel, measure-continuous countable constraint functions. The selector gives the Borel feasible domain and the feasible choice there.

overlap.comparison: The accepted fixed integer-fiber result constructs a particular coupling with uniform source marginals and a root-volume ceiling. It supplies neither measurable selection for arbitrary parameter-dependent marginals and ceilings nor the simultaneous comparison to a prescribed old law.

The accepted same-mark convex-order result concerns two fixed integrated measures on a compact marked relation with one common physical marking map. It does not select a barycentric tuple coupling subject to simultaneous endpoint marginals and output domination.

readability: The common compact output test set can be the union of the old and ceiling supports and the barycentric image of the fixed endpoint product. A joint support relation is transferred when it holds for the feasible choices almost everywhere.

summary: The pointwise marginal, old-law convex-order and ceiling conditions form a countable compact selection problem. The selected kernel retains all three conditions on one full-measure set and integrates them with the parameter.
